newsitem.title: USA: AT&T Q4 wireline, wireless revs rise.
newsitem.headline: AT&T Q4 wireline, wireless revs rise.

text.p: At&T Corp said on Wednesday that wireline services revenue grew three percent in the fourth quarter of 1996 to $11.54 billion, while wireless services revenue grew 18.4 percent to $937 million.

For the quarter, communications services revenue increased $529 million, or 4.3 percent from the same period last year. Communications services revenues include wireline services, wireless services as well as communications products and other services.
Wireless subscribers grew 31.7 perent to 5.2 million from a year ago, including 900,000 digital subscribers.
"We remain committed to growing our core business, investing wisely in the future and ultimately building long-term value for our owners," said chairman Robert Allen.
AT&T said that One Rate, a flat 15 cents per minute long distance calling plan, had been well received and was meeting AT&T's expectation for reducing customer churn.
Financial services had an operating loss of $4 million for the quarter compared with operating profit of $109 million a year ago. Revenues fell 32.3 percent from a year ago.
However this was an improvement from the third quarter 1996 when an operating loss of $35 million was recorded.

The improvement on the third quarter at the unit was due to lower costs, with expenses falling 15 percent. The fall in revenues was caused mainly by a securitization program begun in 1995, which almost doubled securitized receivables to $6.5 billion in 1996.
Total financial services receivables were $13.5 billion on 18.3 million customer accounts at the end of the fourth quarter.

Revenues from communication products and other products, which includes outsourcing and consulting, online and wireless product sales were 17 percent up at $386 million in the quarter from a year ago.
